title: IEEE Ethernet
label: 10 Mb/s
note: The original IEEE 802.3 standard for wired local networks.
culture: Also in 1983: WarGames put dial-up hacking on screen. Its modem connection was a different technology from Ethernet.

title: Fast Ethernet
label: 100 Mb/s
note: A tenfold increase in Ethernet line rate.
culture: The year Toy Story arrived in cinemas—the first feature-length computer-animated film.

title: 56k dial-up · V.90
label: Up to 56 kb/s
note: Downstream maximum; upstream was up to 33.6 kb/s. Actual connections could be slower.
culture: The dial-up internet era of You’ve Got Mail, released in 1998.

title: Gigabit Ethernet
label: 1 Gb/s
note: IEEE 802.3z brings gigabit rates to Ethernet.

title: Wi-Fi · 802.11b
label: 11 Mb/s
note: A nominal wireless link rate, shared over the radio channel—not application throughput.

title: 10 Gigabit Ethernet
label: 10 Gb/s
note: IEEE 802.3ae extends Ethernet to 10 gigabits per second.

title: Starlink optical intersatellite links
label: Up to 200 Gb/s
note: Advertised rate per optical link in Starlink’s 2024 progress report; this is the report date, not the invention date.

title: Appa & Momo · this lab
label: 200 kb/s
note: Short optical tests: 128 / 128 packets across two runs. Useful payload rate ≈18.7 kb/s.
